exposure: socio-demographic variables (e.g., formal education, poverty, hunger)
cohort: 416 pregnant adolescents, aged 13-19 years old, were followed from health centres in the Ashanti Region, Ghana.
finding: Socioeconomic factors such as lack of formal education, high lived poverty index, experiencing hunger, and experiencing illness, along with antenatal care compliance, were identified as significant predictors of preterm birth and low birth weight among pregnant adolescents, while ITN use was associated with reduced odds of LBW.
